subject: Biology
description: Organelle functions, cell types, classic discovery facts

questions.stem: The POWERHOUSE of the cell is:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria — site of aerobic cellular respiration (ATP synthesis). Called 'powerhouse of the cell' (Philip Siekevitz, 1957). Double-membraned, cristae (inner folds), own DNA and ribosomes (endosymbiont theory by Lynn Margulis).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Who FIRST discovered the cell (in 1665) by observing a cork slice?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke — in 'Micrographia' (1665) — coined the term 'cell' for the box-like structures in cork. Leeuwenhoek later (~1674) observed LIVE cells / microorganisms. Schleiden & Schwann formulated the Cell Theory (1838-39); Virchow added 'Omnis cellula e cellula' (1855).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Match the ORGANELLE with its FUNCTION. A. Ribosome.  B. Golgi apparatus.  C. Lysosome.  D. Endoplasmic reticulum. List-II: 1. Protein synthesis.  2. Packaging and sorting of proteins.  3. Intracellular digestion.  4. Transport, synthesis of lipids/steroids.
questions.explanation: Ribosome — translation. Golgi — modification, packaging, shipping. Lysosome — 'suicide bags', hydrolytic enzymes. ER — smooth ER (lipid/steroid synthesis) + rough ER (ribosomes on surface, protein synthesis).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Which of the following cell organelles is ABSENT in ANIMAL cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplast — absent in animal cells (no photosynthesis). Plant cells also have cell wall (cellulose) and large central vacuole that animal cells lack. Conversely, centrioles + lysosomes are typical of animal cells and rare in plants.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The GENETIC MATERIAL in a cell is PRIMARILY located in the:
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic DNA is in the nucleus (as chromatin, condensing to chromosomes during division). Small amounts also in mitochondria (mtDNA) and chloroplasts (cpDNA). Prokaryotes have no true nucleus — DNA floats in nucleoid region.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: The LONGEST cell in the human body is:
questions.explanation: Motor neurons can extend from the lower spinal cord to the foot — up to 1 metre long — the longest cells in the body. Ovum is the LARGEST by volume (~0.1 mm). RBCs are among the smallest at ~7-8 µm. nerve cell.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.stem: Consider the following. 1. Cell wall in plants is made of cellulose; in fungi it is chitin. 2. Ribosomes can be free in the cytoplasm OR bound to the rough ER. 3. Mitochondria have their own DNA and ribosomes, evidence for the endosymbiotic theory. 4. The nucleolus is responsible for DNA replication. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG. The NUCLEOLUS is responsible for RIBOSOMAL RNA synthesis and ribosome subunit assembly, not DNA replication (that happens in the nucleoplasm). 1, 2, 3 are all correct.
